def hydrate_time(nanoseconds, tz=None):

    # Check if `nanoseconds` is a valid value
    if nanoseconds < 0:
        raise ValueError("nanoseconds must be a non-negative integer")

    # Check if `tz` is a valid timezone string
    if tz is not None and not valid_timezone(tz):
        raise ValueError("tz must be a valid timezone string")

    # Convert nanoseconds to seconds
    seconds = nanoseconds // 1000000000

    # Set the timezone
    if tz is None:
        tz = pytz.timezone("UTC")
    elif not isinstance(tz, pytz.timezone):
        tz = pytz.timezone(tz)

    # Hydrate the time
    time = datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, tz=tz)
    return time

depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol

classmethod protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
    """
    Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
    keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
    provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
    depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
    version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

    :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
        version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
    :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
        relevant and supported protocol versions
    :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
    """

    handlers = dict()
    for version in [
        (0, 0),
        (1, 0),
        (1, 1),
        (1, 2),
        (2, 0),
        (3, 0),
        (3, 1),
        (3, 2),
        (3, 3),
        (3, 4),
        (3, 5),
    ]:
        try:
            handler = cls._protocol_handlers[version]
        except KeyError:
            handler = None
        if (
            protocol_version is None or
            protocol_version == version
        ):
            handlers[version] = handler

    if not handlers:
        raise ValueError(
            "Requested protocol version is not supported"
        )

    return handlers

def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
    """
    Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers, keyed by version tuple.
    If an explicit protocol version is provided, the dictionary will contain either
    zero or one items, depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
    version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

    :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol version (e.g. (3, 5))
     or None
    :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all relevant and supported
     protocol versions
    :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
    """
    # We first check if the provided version is a tuple, if so we use it,
    # otherwise we use all available versions
    if isinstance(protocol_version, tuple):
        versions = {protocol_version}
    else:
        versions = set(cls.supported_versions)

    # We now iterate through the supported protocol versions and return a dictionary
    # with each version mapped to the corresponding handler.
    return {version: cls._get_protocol_handler(version) for version in versions}

name: unit_of_work
docstring:
This function is a decorator for transaction functions that allows extra control over how the transaction is carried out.

For example, a timeout may be applied::

    from neo4j import unit_of_work

    @unit_of_work(timeout=100)
    def count_people_tx(tx):
        result = tx.run("MATCH (a:Person) RETURN count(a) AS persons")
        record = result.single()
        return record["persons"]

:param metadata:
    a dictionary with metadata.
    Specified metadata will be attached to the executing transaction and visible in the output of ``dbms.listQueries`` and ``dbms.listTransactions`` procedures.
    It will also get logged to the ``query.log``.
    This functionality makes it easier to tag transactions and is equivalent to ``dbms.setTXMetaData`` procedure, see https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/reference/procedures/ for procedure reference.
:type metadata: dict

:param timeout:
    the transaction timeout in seconds.
    Transactions that execute longer than the configured timeout will be terminated by the database.
    This functionality allows to limit query/transaction execution time.
    Specified timeout overrides the default timeout configured in the database using ``dbms.transaction.timeout`` setting.
    Value should not represent a negative duration.
    A zero duration will make the transaction execute indefinitely.
    None will use the default timeout configured in the database.
:type timeout: float or :const:`None`
code:
def unit_of_work(metadata: dict, timeout: float = None) -> None:
    # If the transaction times out, raise an exception
    if timeout and timeout < 0:
        raise Exception("Transaction timeout must be a positive duration or None")

    # If the transaction times out, raise an exception
    if timeout and timeout > 0 and timeout < transaction_timeout:
        raise Exception("Transaction timeout must be greater than the default timeout")

    # If metadata is provided, attach it to the transaction
    if metadata:
        tx_metadata = metadata

    # If the transaction times out, raise an exception
    if timeout and timeout == 0:
        raise Exception("Transaction timeout must not be 0")

    # Set the transaction timeout to the specified value or the default value if timeout is None
    transaction_timeout = timeout or default_timeout

    # Return a new transaction function that has the same behavior as the original transaction function, but with the specified metadata andtimeout attached
    def decorated_transaction(tx):
        # Attach the metadata to the transaction
        if metadata:
            tx.metadata = metadata

        # Set the transaction timeout
        tx.timeout = transaction_timeout

        # Execute the original transaction function
        with tx.validate():
            tx.run(function)

    return decorated_transaction

def attach_metadata(func):
        # Inner wrapper function that executes the wrapped function
        def wrapper(tx):
            # Set transaction metadata to be visible in query log
            if metadata is not None:
                dbms.setTXMetaData(tx, metadata)
            # Wrap the function in timeout wrapper
            timeout_wrapper = timeout_wrapper(func, timeout)
            # Execute the function with the timeout wrapper
            return timeout_wrapper(tx)
        # Return the inner wrapper
        return wrapper
    # Return the decorated function
    return attach_metadata

def index(self, key):
    """
    Return the index of the given item.

    :param key: a key
    :return: index
    :rtype: int
    """

    # find index of key in list
    for i, item in enumerate(self.data):
        if item == key:
            return i

    # key was not found, return -1
    return -1

def pop_u16(self: Bytearray_struct) -> U16:
    # Check if there are at least 2 bytes of data in the buffer
    if self.length < 2:
        raise ValueError("Buffer contains insufficient data")

    # Read the last two bytes and convert to big-endian 16-bit unsigned integer
    u16 = U16(self.data[self.length - 2:self.length])

    # Decrement the buffer length by 2
    self.length -= 2

    return u16

def pop_u16(self):
    """ Remove the last two bytes of data, returning them as a big-endian
    16-bit unsigned integer.
    """
    if len(self.data) < 2:
        raise IndexError("pop_u16: data length too short")
    value = int.from_bytes(self.data[-2:], "big")
    self.data = self.data[:-2]
    return value

:param dehydration_hooks:
    Hooks to dehydrate types (dict from type (class) to dehydration
    function). Dehydration functions receive the value and returns an
    object of type understood by packstream.
:param hydration_hooks:
    Hooks to hydrate types (mapping from type (class) to
    dehydration function). Dehydration functions receive the value of
    type understood by packstream and are free to return anything.

def discard(self, n=-1, qid=-1, dehydration_hooks=None, hydration_hooks=None, **handlers):
    # Create DISCARD message
    message = Message(DISCARD, n=n, qid=qid, dehydration_hooks=dehydration_hooks, hydration_hooks=hydration_hooks)

    # Append message to output queue
    self.output_queue.append(message)

    # Return Response object with handlers
    return Response(self, message, handlers)

        raise ValueError("Invalid number of records to discard.")

    hydration_hooks = {} if hydration_hooks is None else hydration_hooks

        raise ValueError("Invalid number of records to discard.")
    if qid < 0 or qid >= len(self.query_log):
        raise ValueError("Invalid query ID to discard for.")

    # Discard the specified records
    discarded_records = self.output_queue[-n:]
    self.output_queue = self.output_queue[:-n]

    # Dehydrate the discarded records using the provided dehydration hooks
    for record in discarded_records:
        for type_, dehydrate_fn in dehydration_hooks.items():
            if isinstance(record, type_):
                record = dehydrate_fn(record)
                break

    # Append a DISCARD message to the output queue
    self.logger.info("Discarding records for query ID {}: {}".format(qid, discarded_records))
    self.output_queue.append(("DISCARD", discarded_records))

    for record in discarded_records:
        for type_, hydrate_fn in hydration_hooks.items():
            if isinstance(record, type_):
                record = hydrate_fn(record)
                break

    response = Response(discarded_records, handlers)
    return response

def point_type(name, fields, srid_map):
    """ Dynamically create a Point subclass.

    The point type is a dynamically created subclass of the Point class with the specified name and fields.
    The fields parameter is expected to be a list of field names that will be added as properties to the subclass.
    The srid_map parameter is expected to be a dictionary that maps field names to SRIDs.

    Args:
        name (str): The name of the point type.
        fields (list): The list of fields that will be added as properties to the subclass.
        srid_map (dict): The dictionary that maps field names to SRIDs.

    Returns:
        The dynamically created point type.

    Raises:
        TypeError: Raised if any of the input parameters are not of the expected type.
        ValueError: Raised if the provided field names contain invalid characters or if the provided SRIDs are invalid.

    Examples:
        >>> point_type('PointType', ['x', 'y'], { 'x': 4326, 'y': 4326 })
        <class '__main__.PointType'>
    """
    class PointType(Point):
        def __init__(self, x, y):
            super().__init__(x, y)
            for field in fields:
                setattr(self, field, None)
                srid = srid_map[field]
                if not isinstance(srid, int):
                    raise TypeError(f'SRID for {field} must be an integer, got {srid}.')
                if not 1 <= srid <= 9999:
                    raise ValueError(f'SRID for {field} must be between 1 and 9999, got {srid}.')

    return PointType

def point_type(name, fields, srid_list: list):
    """ Dynamically create a Point subclass.

    :param name: The name of the point type.
    :param fields: A dictionary of fields to be included in the point type.
    :param srid_list: A list of SRID codes for the point type.
    :return: The dynamically created Point subclass.
    """
    class Point(Point):
        def __init__(self, srid, *args, **kwargs):
            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
            self.srid = srid

    for field in fields:
        Point.__init__.__signature__ += Parameter(field, kind=ParamKind.token)

    for srid in srid_list:
        srid_point_cls = type(str(name + str(srid)), (Point,), {})
        globals()[str(name + str(srid))] = srid_point_cls

    return globals()[str(name + str(srid_list[0]))]

def _inline_r_setup(code: str) -> str:
    import rpy2.robjects as robjects
    import rpy2.robjects.conversion as conv

    try:
        # First, try to convert the input string to a proper list of strings
        # that we can pass to R
        code_list = [item.strip() for item in code.splitlines()]

        # Next, create an rpy2 object for each line of R code
        # This will catch any syntax errors in the input string
        lines = [robjects.Rcode(line) for line in code_list]

        # Now, create a global object that will store all the R code
        # This allows us to pass it to R as a single object
        all_lines = robjects.Rvector("All lines", lines)

        # Now, execute the R code using the rpy2.robjects.r function
        # This will catch any runtime errors in the R code
        result = robjects.r(all_lines)

        # Finally, convert the rpy2 object back to a string and return it
        return conv.py2rpy(result).extract()

    except Exception as e:
        # If there was an error, raise a custom exception that includes the
        # error message and the input string that caused it
        raise RSetupError(f"Error while setting up R: {e}")

    """
    Some behaviour of R cannot be configured via env variables, but can

    r_opts_string = "--" + "--".join(r_opts)

def lru_cache(maxsize=128, typed=False):
    """Decorator to wrap a function with a memoizing callable that saves
    up to `maxsize` results based on a Least Recently Used (LRU)
    algorithm.

    Parameters
    ----------
    maxsize : int, optional
        The maximum number of results to store in the cache. By default,
        this is set to 128.
    typed : bool, optional
        Indicates whether the cache uses type-based or non-type-based
        cache keys. False by default.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> @lru_cache(maxsize=5)
    ... def fibonacci(n):
    ...     if n <= 0:
    ...         return 0
    ...     if n == 1:
    ...         return 1
    ...     return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)
    ...
    >>> g = fibonacci(5)
    >>> g = fibonacci(5)
    >>> g = fibonacci(5)
    >>> g = fibonacci(6)
    >>> g = fibonacci(6)
    >>> g = fibonacci(6)
    >>> g = fibonacci(6)
    13
    0
    0
    5
    0
    [13, 8]

    """

    def decorator(func):
        if typed:
            cache = collections.TypedSimpleCache(maxsize)
        else:
            cache = collections.SimpleCache(maxsize)

        def wrap(*args, **kwargs):
            key = (args, frozenset(kwargs.items()))
            if key not in cache:
                cache[key] = func(*args, **kwargs)
            return cache[key]

        wrap.__name__ = func.__name__
        wrap.__doc__ = func.__doc__
        return wrap

    return decorator

def extostr(cls, e, max_level=30, max_path_level=5):
    """
    Format an exception.
    :param e: Any exception instance.
    :type e: Exception
    :param max_level: Maximum call stack level (default 30)
    :type max_level: int
    :param max_path_level: Maximum path level (default 5)
    :type max_path_level: int
    :return The exception readable string
    :rtype str
    """
    # Preliminary checks
    if not isinstance(e, BaseException):
        raise TypeError("'e' must be an exception instance.")
    if not isinstance(max_level, int) or max_level < 0:
        raise ValueError("'max_level' must be a non-negative integer.")
    if not isinstance(max_path_level, int) or max_path_level < 0:
        raise ValueError("'max_path_level' must be a non-negative integer.")

    # Define local variables for the output
    out = []
    level = 0
    frames = inspect.getouterframes(inspect.currentframe())

    # Iterate through each frame in the call stack
    while True:
        frame = frames.pop(0)
        out.append(f"{level} - {frame.filename}:{frame.lineno}")
        if level >= max_level:
            break
        level += 1
        if level >= max_path_level:
            break

    # Return the output
    return "".join(out)

    if len(path) > max_path_level:
        path = path[:max_path_level] + ["..."]
    path.reverse()
    return "(%s) %s" % ("/".join(path), msg)

def _legacy_mergeOrderings(orderings):
    """Merge multiple orderings so that within-ordering order is preserved

    Orderings are constrained in such a way that if an object appears
    in two or more orderings, then the suffix that begins with the
    object must be in both orderings.

    Args:
        orderings (list of lists of strings):
            The orderings to be merged.

    Returns:
        list of strings:
            The merged orderings.

    Raises:
        ValueError:
            If the orderings are not compatible (i.e., if the suffix
            that begins with an object is not in all orderings that
            contain the object).

    Examples:
        >>> _mergeOrderings([
        ... ['x', 'y', 'z'],
        ... ['q', 'z'],
        ... [1, 3, 5],
        ... ['z']
        ... ])
        ['x', 'y', 'q', 1, 3, 5, 'z']

    """
    merged_ordering = []
    for ordering in orderings:
        for o in ordering:
            if o not in merged_ordering:
                merged_ordering.append(o)
    return merged_ordering

def _normalizeargs(sequence, output=None):
    """Normalize declaration arguments

    Given a sequence of objects, normalizes them by expanding any tuples or
    single interfaces into the corresponding Declarions or implements specs.

    Args:
        sequence (list): Sequence of objects to normalize
        output (list, optional): List to store the normalized objects. If not
            provided, a new list will be created. Defaults to None.

    Returns:
        list: The normalized list of objects
    """
    if output is None:
        output = []

    for arg in sequence:
        if isinstance(arg, tuple):
            output += arg
        elif isinstance(arg, str):
            output.append(arg)
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"Invalid argument type: {type(arg)}")

    return output

def fill(self, coord: tuple, weight: int = 1) -> None:
    """
    Fill the histogram at the given coordinate with the given weight.

    Args:
        coord: The coordinate to fill.
        weight: The weight to fill with.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    if not isinstance(coord, tuple) or len(coord) != 2:
        raise TypeError("Expected coordinate to be a tuple of length 2.")
    if not isinstance(weight, int):
        raise TypeError("Expected weight to be an integer.")

    x, y = coord
    if x < 0 or y < 0 or x >= self.width or y >= self.height:
        return

    self.data[x][y] += weight

def generate_default_observer_schema_dict(manifest_dict, first_level=False):
    """This function generates a default observer schema dictionary depending on supplied manifest dictionary.

    Args:
        manifest_dict (dict): Partial Kubernetes resource
        first_level (bool, optional): Option to indicate root of observer_schema of a K8s resource

    Returns:
        dict: Generated partial observer_schema dictionary

    """
    # Create new dictionary from manifest dict and populate with None for any non-list, non-dict values
    observer_schema = {key: None for key in manifest_dict}

    # If key exists in manifest dict and is a list or dict, iterate and use recursive function
    for key, value in manifest_dict.items():
        if isinstance(value, (list, dict)):
            observer_schema[key] = generate_default_observer_schema_dict(value, first_level)

    # If first_level is True, overwrite values of identifying fields with values from manifest dict
    if first_level:
        observer_schema["name"] = manifest_dict["metadata"]["name"]
        observer_schema["namespace"] = manifest_dict["metadata"]["namespace"]
        observer_schema["labels"] = manifest_dict["metadata"]["labels"]
        observer_schema["annotations"] = manifest_dict["metadata"]["annotations"]

    return observer_schema

def generate_default_observer_schema(app):
    # Observer schemas are used to define the shape of the data that Krake can receive from
    # each Kubernetes resource in the application's manifest.
    # In this method, we generate a default observer schema for each resource that
    # hasn't already been defined in the Kubernetes Custom Resource Definition (CRD)
    # or by the Krake user.
    # The default schema assumes that the resource data will be a JSON object with
    # a single "status" field, which has a sub-object called "conditions".
    # The "conditions" object is a list of condition objects, each of which has
    # fields for the condition type and the current status of the corresponding resource.
    # The "resources" field is a list of the Kubernetes resources that should be observed
    # for this application.
    # The "path" field specifies the path to the resource data in the application manifest.
    # The "mapping" field gives a mapping between the resource fields and the observed
    # data fields.
    # The "filter" field gives a list of condition types that should be observed. If None,
    # all conditions are included.
    # The "pause" field determines whether observing resources of this type should be paused
    # by default.

    schema = {
        "resources": [],
        "path": None,
        "mapping": None,
        "filter": None,
        "pause": None,
    }

    # Generate a list of resources that have not already been defined in the CRD
    # or by the Krake user.
    resources = Krake.data.kubernetes.get_resource_names(app)
    for resource in resources:
        # Check if the resource has already been defined in the CRD or Kube.yaml file.
        if resource not in app.observer.resources:
            # Add the resource to the schema.
            schema["resources"].append(resource)

    return schema

    if app is None:

    # Extract the manifest from the application
    manifest = app.spec.manifest

    # Initialize the observer schema
    default_observer_schema = KrakeDefaultObserverSchema()

    # Iterate over each Kubernetes resource in the manifest
    for resource in manifest.items:
        # If a custom observer schema has not been specified for this resource, use the default one
        if resource.obj.metadata.annotations.get("krake.endpoints.controlplane.operator.krake.io/observer-schema") is None:
            default_observer_schema.add_resource_to_schema(resource)

    # Return the generated observer schema
    return default_observer_schema

    # Initialize an empty list to store the formatted SQL queries
    formatted_sql_list = []
    # Iterate over the many params
    for params in many_params:
        # Check if the param is a mapping or a sequence
        if isinstance(params, Mapping):
            # Convert the mapping to a list of tuples and use it to format the SQL query
            formatted_sql_list.append(tuple(params.items()))
        elif isinstance(params, Sequence):
            # Convert the sequence to a list and use it to format the SQL query
            formatted_sql_list.append(list(params))
        else:
            # Raise a TypeError if the param is not a mapping or a sequence
            raise TypeError("Invalid type for params. Must be a mapping or a sequence.")
    # Join the formatted SQL queries into a single string
    formatted_sql = ", ".join(formatted_sql_list)
    # Return the formatted SQL string and the formatted params list

def validate(self, path):
    """
    Validate OCFL object at path or pyfs root.

    Returns True if valid (warnings permitted), False otherwise.
    """
    # Step 1: Check if the path is a valid path string
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise ValueError("Invalid path type")

    # Step 2: Check if the path exists and is a directory
    if not os.path.exists(path) or not os.path.isdir(path):
        raise FileNotFoundError("Path does not exist or is not a directory")

    # Step 3: Check if the path contains an OCFL layout
    if not os.path.join(path, "info.json") or not os.path.join(path, "v1"):
        raise ValueError("Path does not contain an OCFL layout")

    # Step 4: Check if the info.json file is valid
    with open(os.path.join(path, "info.json"), "r") as f:
        info = json.load(f)

    if "valid" not in info or not info["valid"]:
        raise ValueError("Info.json file is invalid")

    # Step 5: Check if the v1 directory contains files that match the required naming convention
    files = os.listdir(os.path.join(path, "v1"))
    pattern = r"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}.par$"

    for file in files:
        match = re.match(pattern, file)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError("File does not match required naming convention")

    return True

    metadata_dir = root_dir / "_metadata"
    metadata_filename = metadata_dir / "ocfl_object_v1.0.json"

        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("object is not a directory")

    # validate the folder in the object directory
    folder = os.listdir(object_dir)
    if not len(folder) == 1 or not os.path.isdir(folder[0]):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no subfolders or multiple subfolders found in object directory")

    # validate the metadata directory
    if not os.path.isdir(metadata_dir):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no metadata directory found")

    # validate the metadata file
    if not os.path.isfile(metadata_filename):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no metadata file found")

    # validate the metadata JSON
    if not metadata.has("id"):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no id found in metadata")
    elif not metadata.has("created"):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no created field found in metadata")
    elif not isinstance(metadata.get("created"), str):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("created is not a string")
    elif not isinstance(metadata.get("created"), datetime):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("created is not a datetime object")
    elif not metadata.get("created").time() < root_datetime.time():
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("created timestamp is not before root timestamp")

    version = metadata.get("version")
    version_dir = root_dir / "v" + str(version)
    if not os.path.isdir(version_dir):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no version directory found")

    # validate the inventory directory
    inventory_dir = version_dir / "inventory"
    if not os.path.isdir(inventory_dir):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no inventory directory found")

    # validate the content file
    content_file = inventory_dir / "content"
    if not os.path.isfile(content_file):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no content file found")

    # validate the inventory file
    inventory_file = inventory_dir / "inventory"
    if not os.path.isfile(inventory_file):
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("no inventory file found")

    # validate the content
    content = json.loads(content_file.open().read())
    if not metadata.get("content") == content:
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("content doesn't match metadata")

    # validate the inventory
    inventory = json.loads(inventory_file.open().read())
    if not metadata.get("inventory") == inventory:
        raise OcfMethod.OcfError("inventory doesn't match metadata")

    # return True if all validation checks pass
    return True

def status_str(self, prefix=''):
    """
    Return a string representation of the validation log, with an optional prefix.
    The string consists of a newline character (`\n`)-separated list of
    status messages, where each message consists of a type and a message
    separated by a space. The type is one of the following:

    * `"m":` indicates a new entry, which will be followed by a message
    * `--`: indicates that no message is available
    * `"bp":` indicates that a breakpoint was past, with the message following

    Args:
        prefix (str, optional): a string to be prepended to the output

    Returns:
        str: a string representation of the validation log
    """

    status_lines = []
    for entry in self.entries:
        if entry.type == 'm':
            status_lines.append(f'{prefix}{entry.type}: {entry.message}')
        elif entry.type == '--':
            status_lines.append(f'{prefix}{entry.type}')
        elif entry.type == 'bp':
            status_lines.append(f'{prefix}{entry.type}: {entry.message}')
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'Invalid entry type: {entry.type}')
    return '\n'.join(status_lines)

    :param extract_spec_version: Whether to extract the specification version from the type value, defaults to False
    :type extract_spec_version: bool, optional
    :return: Validation result
    :rtype: bool
    """
    # Extract the type value if extract_spec_version is True
    type_value = inventory.type if extract_spec_version else None

    # Initialize the validation result
    result = False

    # Validate the type value if it is not None
    if type_value is not None:
        # Validate the type value against the known specification versions
        if type_value in self.spec_versions:
            # Validate the inventory based on the identified specification version
            result = self._validate_inventory(inventory, type_value)
        else:
            # If the type value is not in the known specification versions, then the inventory is invalid
            result = False
    else:
        # If there is no type value, then the inventory is invalid
        result = False

    # Return the validation result
    return result

def check_digests_present_and_used(manifest_files, digests_used):
    """
    Checks all digests in the given manifest files are present and used.

    Args:
        manifest_files (list): A list of manifest file paths.
        digests_used (list): A list of digest types.

    Returns:
        list: A list of manifest file paths with digests missing or unused.
    """
    # Initialize a list to store missing or unused digests
    missing_or_unused_digests = []

    # Iterate over the manifest files
    for manifest in manifest_files:
        # Open the manifest file for reading
        with open(manifest, "r") as f:
            # Read the manifest file contents
            manifest_contents = f.read()

        # Split the manifest file contents by line breaks
        manifest_lines = manifest_contents.splitlines()

        # Iterate over the manifest lines
        for line in manifest_lines:
            # If the line contains a digest
            if "Digest" in line:
                # Split the line into the digest type and the digest string
                digest_type, digest_string = line.split("=")

                # If the digest type is not in the list of digests used
                if digest_type not in digests_used:
                    # Add the manifest file path to the list of missing or unused digests
                    missing_or_unused_digests.append(manifest)

                    # Break out of the loop
                    break

    # Return the list of missing or unused digests
    return missing_or_unused_digests

def validate_as_prior_version(self, prior: InventoryValidator):
    """
    Check that prior is a valid prior version of the current inventory object.

    Args:
        prior (InventoryValidator): The prior version of the inventory object.

    Returns:
        bool: True if prior is a valid prior version of the current inventory object, otherwise False.
    """
    if not isinstance(prior, InventoryValidator):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input type for prior. Expected InventoryValidator, got {}".format(type(prior)))
    if not prior.is_valid():
        return False
    # Check if prior inventory has same item IDs as current inventory
    if set(prior.get_item_ids()) != set(self.get_item_ids()):
        return False
    # Check if prior inventory has same inventory info as current inventory
    for item_id in prior.get_item_ids():
        if prior.get_item(item_id).get_info() != self.get_item(item_id).get_info():
            return False
    # All checks passed, prior is a valid prior version of the current inventory
    return True

def get_logical_path_map(inventory, version):
    # 1. create an empty dictionary to store the output
    logical_path_map = {}

    # 2. iterate over the content items in the inventory
    for content_item in inventory.content_items:
        # 3. get the logical path of the content item
        logical_path = content_item.logical_path

        # 4. check if the logical path is already in the map
        if logical_path not in logical_path_map:
            # 5. if not, create a new key with an empty set
            logical_path_map[logical_path] = set()

        # 6. add the content_file to the set associated with the logical path
        logical_path_map[logical_path].add(content_item.content_file)

    # 7. return the map
    return logical_path_map

def _group_files_by_xml_filename(xml_filename, files):
    """
    Group files by their XML basename.

    Groups files by their XML basename and returns data in dict format.

    Parameters
    ----------
    xml_filename : str
        XML filename
    files : list
        list of files in the folder or zipfile

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        key: name of the XML files
        value: Package
    """

    # Initialize an empty dictionary to store the grouped files
    grouped_files = {}

    # Loop through the list of files
    for file in files:
        # Get the basename of the file
        basename = os.path.basename(file)

        # Check if the file is an XML file
        if basename.endswith(".xml"):
            # Add the file to the dictionary using the basename as the key
            grouped_files[basename] = file

    return grouped_files

def select_filenames_by_prefix(prefix, files):
    """
    Get files which belongs to a document package.

    Retorna os arquivos da lista `files` cujos nomes iniciam com `prefix`

    Parameters
    ----------
    prefix : str
        Filename prefix
    files : str list
        Files paths
    Returns
    -------
    list
        files paths which basename files matches to prefix
    """
    # Return an empty list if the file list is empty or the prefix is invalid
    if not files or not prefix or prefix == "":
        return []

    # Initialize an empty list to store the selected files
    selected_files = []

    # Loop through each file in the file list
    for file in files:
        # Check if the file's basename starts with the prefix
        if file.split("/")[-1].startswith(prefix):
            # Add the file to the selected files list
            selected_files.append(file)

    # Return the selected files list
    return selected_files

def _eval_file(prefix, file_path):
    import os
    import re

    # Get the file name without extension
    file_name = os.path.splitext(file_path)[0]

    # Check if file name starts with prefix
    if not file_name.startswith(prefix):
        raise ValueError(f"File name {file_name} does not start with prefix {prefix}")

    # Get the file extension
    file_ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1]

    # Check if file extension is valid
    valid_extensions = ['.xml', '.jpg', '.png']
    if file_ext not in valid_extensions:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid file extension {file_ext}")

    # Get the file folder
    folder_name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(file_path))

    # Check if folder name is valid
    valid_folders = ['asset', 'rendition']
    if folder_name not in valid_folders:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid folder name {folder_name}")

    # Return the file type and the folder
    return {
        'type': folder_name,
        'file': file_path
    }

def _eval_file(prefix, filename, file_folder):
    # Extract the file extension from the filename
    extension = os.path.splitext(filename)[1]

    # Check if the file extension is a recognized asset or rendition extension
    if extension not in ('xml', 'json', 'txt'):
        raise ValueError(f'Invalid file extension {extension}')

    # Update the packages dictionary with the file path and type
    packages[prefix]['file_path'] = os.path.join(file_folder, filename)
    packages[prefix]['type'] = 'asset' if extension == 'xml' else 'rendition'

    return packages

def add_rendition(self, lang, file_path):
    """
    Adds a new rendition to the document for the specified language.

    :param lang: The language for the new rendition.
    :type lang: str
    :param file_path: The path to the file that contains the new rendition.
    :type file_path: str
    """
    try:
        language = self.languages[lang]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid language '{lang}'")

    if not os.path.isfile(file_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File '{file_path}' not found")

    rendition_path = Path(file_path).stem + f"-{lang}.pdf"
    language["rendition"] = rendition_path
    self.save_languages()

def add_rendition(self, lang, file_path):
    """
    Adds a rendition to the document.

    Args:
        lang (str): The language code of the rendition.
        file_path (str): The path to the rendition file.

    Returns:
        None

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the language code is not valid.
        FileNotFoundError: If the file path does not exist.
        ExtensionNotSupportedError: If the file extension is not supported.
    """
    if lang not in self._languages:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid language code: {lang}")
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {file_path}")
    if os.path.splitext(file_path)[1] not in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
        raise ExtensionNotSupportedError(f"File extension not supported: {os.path.splitext(file_path)[1]}")
    self._renditions[lang] = file_path

    """
    Add a rendition to the translation dictionary.

    Args:
        lang (str): The language code of the rendition.
        file_path (str): The path to the rendition file.

    Returns:
        bool: Whether the rendition was successfully added.
    """
    if lang in self.translations.keys():
        raise ValueError("Rendition already exists for language {lang}")
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        raise ValueError("Rendition file {file_path} does not exist")
    self.translations[lang] = file_path
    return True

def fix_namespace_prefix(content):
    # Split the content into individual lines
    lines = content.splitlines()

    # This list will hold the fixed lines
    fixed_lines = []

    for line in lines:
        # Check if the line contains the prefix 'w:st="'
        if 'w:st="' in line:
            # Replace the 'w:st="' prefix with 'w-st="'
            fixed_line = line.replace('w:st="', 'w-st="')
        else:
            # The line does not contain the prefix, so leave it as it is
            fixed_line = line

        # Add the fixed line to the list of fixed lines
        fixed_lines.append(fixed_line)

    # Return the fixed content
    return "\n".join(fixed_lines)

def fix_namespace_prefix_w(content):
    """
    Convert os textos cujo padrão é `w:st="` em `w-st="`

    # Convert all instances of 'w:st="' to 'w-st="'
    content = content.replace('w:st="', 'w-st="')
    return content

def fix_namespace_prefix_w(content):
    return content.replace('w:st=\\"', 'w-st=\\"')

Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the

occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).

def _fromutc(self, dt):
    """
    Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
    timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

    Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
    datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the
    datetime is ambiguous and in a "fold" state (e.g. if it's the first
    occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).

    :param dt:
        A timezone-aware :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
    """
    from datetime import datetime
    from dateutil.tz import tzutc, tzlocal
    from dateutil.tz import tzfile
    from dateutil.tz import tzwin, tzwinlocal, tzwincompressed
    from dateutil.tz import tzdata   

    # Error handling
    if type(dt) != datetime.datetime:
        raise TypeError("Argument must be a datetime.datetime object!")   
    elif dt.tzinfo is not None:
        raise TypeError("The datetime object may not be tz-aware!")
    else:
        new_dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=self)
        #check for time zone error
        hourDiff = abs(new_dt.hour - self.nowInPST().hour)
        if hourDiff > 1:
            raise ValueError("Incorrect time zone detected!")   
        return new_dt

def _fromutc(self, dt):
    # Determine if the given datetime is ambiguous
    if dt.tzinfo._is_dst(dt):
        # If the given datetime is ambiguous, return None
        return None
    # Calculate the new timezone
    new_tz = timezone(dt.tzinfo.utcoffset(dt))
    # Convert the datetime to the new timezone
    new_dt = dt.astimezone(new_tz)
    # Return the new timezone-aware datetime
    return new_dt

    """
    Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
    timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

    Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
    datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the
    datetime is ambiguous and in a "fold" state (e.g. if it's the first
    occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).

    :param dt:
        A timezone-aware :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
    """
    # Check if the datetime object is timezone-aware
    if not dt.tzinfo:
        raise ValueError("Datetime object is not timezone-aware")

    # Get the new timezone
    new_tz = self.tzinfo

    # Convert the datetime to the new timezone using a naive conversion
    new_dt = dt.astimezone(new_tz)

    # Check if the datetime is ambiguous
    if new_dt.is_ambiguous():
        if new_dt.is_fold:
            # If the datetime is in a "fold" state, find the next occurrence
            # of the ambiguous datetime and return it
            new_dt = new_dt.replace(fold=False)
        else:
            # If the datetime is not in a "fold" state, find the previous
            # occurrence of the ambiguous datetime and return it
            new_dt = new_dt.replace(fold=True)

    return new_dt

def normalized(self):
    """
    Return a version of this object represented entirely using integer
    values for the relative attributes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any of the relative attributes, such as years, months, days, hours, minutes, or seconds,
                    exceeds the maximum integer value.
    """
    # Create a copy of the input object
    normalized_obj = copy.deepcopy(self)

    # Normalize the relative attributes using integer division (//)
    normalized_obj.years = int(normalized_obj.years)
    normalized_obj.months = int(normalized_obj.months)
    normalized_obj.days = int(normalized_obj.days)
    normalized_obj.hours = int(normalized_obj.hours)
    normalized_obj.minutes = int(normalized_obj.minutes)
    normalized_obj.seconds = int(normalized_obj.seconds)

    # Check for overflow for each attribute
    if (normalized_obj.years >= 1000000000) or (normalized_obj.months >= 1000000000) or (normalized_obj.days >= 1000000000) or \
            (normalized_obj.hours >= 1000000000) or (normalized_obj.minutes >= 1000000000) or (normalized_obj.seconds >= 1000000000):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input. Relative attributes exceeded maximum integer value.")

    return normalized_obj

def normalized(self: relativedelta) -> relativedelta:
    """
    Return a version of this object represented entirely using integer
    values for the relative attributes.

    >>> relativedelta(days=1.5, hours=2).normalized()
    relativedelta(days=+1, hours=+14)
    """
    normalized_delta = relativedelta()
    for attr in (
        "years",
        "months",
        "days",
        "hours",
        "minutes",
        "seconds",
        "microseconds",
    ):
        value = getattr(self, attr)
        if value:
            setattr(normalized_delta, attr, int(value))
    return normalized_delta

def validate_version_inventories(version_dirs):
    """Validate the version inventories in the given version directories.

    For each version directory, validate that it has an inventory file and that its content digest matches that of the root inventory file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    version_dirs : list of str
        List of version directory names.

    Returns
    -------
    boolean
        True if all inventory files are valid, False otherwise.

    Raises
    ------
    FileNotFoundError
        If an inventory file for a version directory is not found.
    IOError
        If there is an error reading or writing to the inventory file for a version directory.
    """
    # Create a list to store the content digests for all version directories
    content_digests = []

    # Loop through each version directory in the version directories parameter
    for version_dir in version_dirs:
        # Get the inventory file path for the version directory
        inventory_file_path = os.path.join(version_dir, "inventory.txt")

        # Check if the inventory file exists for the version directory
        if not os.path.isfile(inventory_file_path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Inventory file for version {version_dir} not found")

        # Open the inventory file for the version directory and read its content
        with open(inventory_file_path, "r") as inventory_file:
            content_digest = inventory_file.read().strip()

        # Add the content digest to the list of content digests for all version directories
        content_digests.append(content_digest)

    # Check if the content digest for the root inventory file is in the list of content digests for all version directories
    if content_digest_root not in content_digests:
        return False

    # Check if the content digests for all version directories are different from those in the root inventory file
    for content_digest in content_digests:
        if content_digest == content_digest_root:
            return False

    # If all inventory files are valid and their content digests are different from those in the root inventory file, return True
    return True

name: deep_merge_nodes
docstring:
Given a nested borgmatic configuration data structure as a list of tuples in the form of:

    (
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.ScalarNode as a key,
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.MappingNode or other Node as a value,
    ),

... deep merge any node values corresponding to duplicate keys and return the result. If
there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode values (e.g., integers or strings), the last
of the values wins.

For instance, given node values of:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='7')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

... the returned result would be:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

The purpose of deep merging like this is to support, for instance, merging one borgmatic
configuration file into another for reuse, such that a configuration section ("retention",
etc.) does not completely replace the corresponding section in a merged file.

name: deep_merge_nodes
docstring:
Given a nested borgmatic configuration data structure as a list of tuples in the form of:

    (
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.ScalarNode as a key,
        ruamel.yaml.nodes.MappingNode or other Node as a value,
    ),

... deep merge any node values corresponding to duplicate keys and return the result. If
there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode values (e.g., integers or strings), the last
of the values wins.

For instance, given node values of:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='7')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

... the returned result would be:

    [
        (
            ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
            MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                ),
                (
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                    ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                ),
            ]),
        ),
    ]

The purpose of deep merging like this is to support, for instance, merging one borgmatic
configuration file into another for reuse, such that a configuration section ("retention",
etc.) does not completely replace the corresponding section in a merged file.
code:
def deep_merge_nodes(nodes):
    '''
    Given a list of tuples of (key node, value node), deep merge any node values corresponding
    to duplicate keys and return the result. If there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode
    values (e.g., integers or strings), the last of the values wins.
    '''
    # Initialize result list
    result = []

    # Iterate over each node tuple
    for key_node, value_node in nodes:
        # Check if current key node is already in result list
        for i, (result_key_node, _) in enumerate(result):
            # If key nodes match, deep merge value nodes and update result at that index
            if key_node == result_key_node:
                result[i] = (result_key_node, deep_merge_nodes((value_node, result_value_node)))
                break
        # If key node is not in result list, add entire node tuple to result
        else:
            result.append((key_node, value_node))

    return result

def parse_arguments(*unparsed_arguments):
    """Parse command-line arguments from unparsed_arguments
    :param unparsed_arguments: command-line arguments
    :return: a dictionary mapping from subparser name (or "global") to an argparse.Namespace instance
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Parse command-line arguments")
    parser.add_argument("n", type=int, help="Number of arguments to parse")
    parser.add_argument("args", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, help="Arguments to parse")
    args = parser.parse_args(unparsed_arguments)
    arg_dict = {}
    for arg in args:
        if arg.startswith("--"):
            key, value = arg.split("=")
            arg_dict[key[2:]] = value
    return arg_dict

def parse_arguments(*unparsed_arguments):
    # Initialize the argument parser and add subparsers
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="subparser")

    # Add a global parser for arguments that do not have a specific subparser
    global_parser = subparsers.add_parser("global", add_help=False)

    # Add subparsers for each subcommand
    subparsers.add_parser("subcommand1")
    subparsers.add_parser("subcommand2")

    # Parse the arguments
    args = vars(parser.parse_args(unparsed_arguments))

    # If the subparser is not specified, set the "global" subparser as the default
    if "subparser" not in args:
        args["subparser"] = "global"

    # Return the parsed arguments
    return args

def paging(response, max_results):
    page = 1
    page_size = max_results
    pages_count = math.ceil(len(response) / max_results)
    while page <= pages_count:
        start_index = (page - 1) * max_results
        end_index = min(page * max_results, len(response))
        page_list = response[start_index:end_index]
        page += 1
        yield page_list

def paging(response, max_results):
    # Iterator to keep track of current element
    iterator = 0

    # List to store responses
    response_list = []

    # Iterate over each item in the response
    for item in response:
        # If the response is not yet full, add the item to the response list
        if len(response_list) < max_results:
            response_list.append(item)
        # Otherwise, yield the current response list and clear it
        else:
            yield response_list
            response_list = []

    # If there are any remaining items in the response, yield the remaining items
    if response_list:
        yield response_list

    # If there are no remaining items in the response, yield an empty list
    if not response_list:
        yield []

    # Return the generator object
    return response_list

def paging(response, max_results):
    """Returns WAPI response page by page

    Args:
        response (list): WAPI response.
        max_results (int): Maximum number of objects to be returned in one page.
    Returns:
        Generator object with WAPI response split page by page.
    """
    if not response:  # Handles potential empty response

    Parameters:

    Returns:
        list of tuples: The 3 points for each vertex.
    """

    if not all(len(vertex) == 2 for vertex in vertices):
        raise ValueError("Vertices must be a list of 2-tuples.")

        raise ValueError("Vertices must be a list of unique 2-tuples.")

    # Initialize the list of 3-tuples

                        vertices[(vertices.index(vertex) + 1) % len(vertices)]]

        # Add the 3-tuple for the current vertex
        three_tuples.append((vertex, adj_vertices[0], adj_vertices[1]))

    return three_tuples

def int_to_string(number: int, alphabet: List[str], padding: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    The output has the most significant digit first.
    """
    # Convert the number to a list of digits
    digits = list(str(number))

    # Pad the digits with leading 0s if necessary
    if padding is not None and len(digits) < padding:
        digits = [0] * (padding - len(digits)) + digits

    # Convert the digits to letters using the given alphabet
    letters = [alphabet[int(digit)] for digit in digits]

    # Reverse the letters to get the most significant digit first
    letters.reverse()

    # Join the letters to form the final string
    return "".join(letters)

def int_to_string(number: int, alphabet: List[str], padding: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    Args:
        number (int): The number to convert.
        alphabet (List[str]): The alphabet to use for conversion.
        padding (Optional[int]): The number of digits to which to pad the output.

    Returns:
        str: The input number converted to a string.

    Examples:
        >>> int_to_string(123, ['a', 'b', 'c'])
        3b2
        >>> int_to_string(1234, ['a', 'b', 'c'])
        4c3b
        >>> int_to_string(1234, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'])
        4d3c
    """
    if not (isinstance(number, int) and isinstance(alphabet, list)):
        raise ValueError("number and alphabet must be an integer and a list")

    if not all(isinstance(letter, str) for letter in alphabet):
        raise ValueError("alphabet must be a list of strings")

    if len(alphabet) != 4:
        raise ValueError("alphabet must have exactly 4 elements")

    if padding is not None and not isinstance(padding, int):
        raise ValueError("padding must be an integer")

    if number < 0 or number >= 1000:
        raise ValueError("number must be in the range [0, 1000)")

    digits = []
    while number > 0:
        digits.append(alphabet[number % len(alphabet)])
        number = number // len(alphabet)
    if padding is not None:
        digits = [alphabet[0]] * padding + digits
    return "".join(reversed(digits))

def get_repo_archive(url: str, destination_path: Path) -> Path:
    """
    Given an url and a destination path, retrieve and extract .tar.gz archive
    which contains 'desc' file for each package.
    Each .tar.gz archive corresponds to an Arch Linux repo ('core', 'extra', 'community').

    Args:
        url: url of the .tar.gz archive to download
        destination_path: the path on disk where to extract archive

    Returns:
        a directory Path where the archive has been extracted to.
    """
    # Parse URL to extract filename and repo name
    parsed_data = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)
    filename = os.path.basename(parsed_data.path)
    repo_name = filename.split('.')[0]

    # Download archive and extract to destination path
    archive_path = os.path.join(destination_path, filename)
    response = requests.get(url, allow_redirects=True)
    with open(archive_path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(response.content)
    with tarfile.open(archive_path, 'r:gz') as tf:
        tf.extractall(destination_path)

    # Return Path of the extracted directory
    return os.path.join(destination_path, repo_name)

        raise ValueError("Archive path does not exist")
    if not os.path.exists(tmp_path):
        raise ValueError("Temp path does not exist")
    ext = os.path.splitext(archive_path)[1]
    if ext not in [".zip", ".tar.gz"]:
        raise ValueError("Invalid archive type")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="git-") as tmp_dir:
        subprocess.check_call(["tar", "xvfz", archive_path, "-C", tmp_path])
        repo_path = os.path.join(tmp_path, tmp_dir, filename or os.path.basename(archive_path).replace(ext, ""))

        subprocess.check_call(["git", "add", "."], cwd=repo_path)

def oneline(script, separator=" && "):
    """
    converts a script to one line command.
    THis is useful to run a single ssh command and pass a one line script.

    :param script:
    :return:
    """

    converts a script to one line command.

def _resolve_string(matcher):
    '''
    Get the value from environment given a matcher containing a name and an optional default value.
    If the variable is not defined in environment and no default value is provided, an Error is raised.
    '''
    name = matcher.group('name')
    default = matcher.group('default')
    value = os.environ[name] if name in os.environ else None
    if value == None and default == None:
        raise Error('Variable ' + name + ' is not defined in environment, and no default value is provided.')
    return value if value != None else default

def _parse_image_ref(image_href: str) -> Tuple[str, str, bool]:
    """Parse an image href into composite parts.

    :param image_href: href of an image
    :returns: a tuple of the form (image_id, netloc, use_ssl)
    :raises ValueError:

    """
    if not isinstance(image_href, str):
        raise ValueError("image_href must be a string")

    # Split the image href into its parts
    parts = image_href.split("://")
    if len(parts) != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Image href {image_href} is malformed")

    # Check if SSL is used
    use_ssl = parts[0] == "https"

    # Extract the hostname and path
    netloc, path = parts[1].split("/", 1)

    # Extract the image id
    try:
        image_id = path.lstrip("/").split("/")[0]
    except IndexError:
        raise ValueError(f"Image href {image_href} is malformed")

    return image_id, netloc, use_ssl

    Iterate over a string list and remove trailing os seperator characters.

    is removed.

    processed_list = []

def run_command(commands, args, cwd=None, verbose=False, hide_stderr=False, env=None):
    """
    Call the given command(s).

    Parameters
    ----------
    commands : str or list of str
        Command to call or list of commands to call.
    args : list of str
        Arguments to pass to the command.
    cwd : str, optional
        Current working directory of the command, by default None
    verbose : bool, optional
        Whether to print the command to the console, by default False
    hide_stderr : bool, optional
        Whether to discard the subprocess's stderr, by default False
    env : dict, optional
        Environment variables to set for the subprocess, by default None

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The exit code of the command.
    """
    if isinstance(commands, (list, tuple)):
        commands = " ".join(commands)

    options = {}
    if cwd:
        options["cwd"] = cwd
    if hide_stderr:
        options["stderr"] = subprocess.DEVNULL
    if env:
        options["env"] = env

    if verbose:
        print(f"{commands} {' '.join(args)}")

    proc = subprocess.run(commands, *args, **options)
    return proc.returncode

def run_command(commands, args, cwd=None, verbose=False, hide_stderr=False, env=None):
    """Call the given command(s)."""
    # Initialize parameters
    commands = commands.strip().lower()
    commands = commands.split(" ")
    args = args.strip().lower()
    args = args.split(" ")
    cwd = cwd.strip().lower()
    verbose = verbose.lower()
    hide_stderr = hide_stderr.lower()
    env = env.strip().lower()

    # Validate input parameters
    if commands is None or not isinstance(commands, list):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: commands")
    if args is None or not isinstance(args, list):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: args")
    if cwd is not None and not isinstance(cwd, str):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: cwd")
    if verbose not in (True, False):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: verbose")
    if hide_stderr not in (True, False):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: hide_stderr")
    if env is not None and not isinstance(env, dict):
        raise ValueError("Invalid input: env")

    # Build the subprocess arguments
    subprocess_args = {
        "args": args,
        "cwd": cwd,
        "env": env,
        "stdout": subprocess.PIPE,
        "stderr": subprocess.PIPE if hide_stderr else subprocess.STDOUT,
        "universal_newlines": True,
        "bufsize": 1,
        "shell": False
    }

    # Run the command
    try:
        process = subprocess.Popen(commands, **subprocess_args)
        stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
        return_code = process.returncode
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        raise RuntimeError("Command failed with non-zero exit code") from e

    # Print output if verbose is True
    if verbose:
        print(f"Command: {commands}")
        print(f"Args: {args}")
        print(f"Cwd: {cwd}")
        print(f"Verbose: {verbose}")
        print(f"Return code: {return_code}")
        print(f"Silent: {hide_stderr}")
        print(f"Stdout: {stdout}")
        print(f"Stderr: {stderr}")

    # Raise an exception if the command fails
    if return_code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command '{commands}' failed with non-zero exit code: {return_code}")

    return return_code

def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
    """ Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
    keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
    provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
    depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
    version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

    :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
        version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
    :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
        relevant and supported protocol versions
    :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
    """
    if protocol_version is None:
        return cls._handlers
    if not isinstance(protocol_version, tuple):
        raise TypeError("'protocol_version' must be a tuple")
    return {protocol_version: cls._handlers[protocol_version]}

def from_raw_values(cls, values):
    """
    Create a Bookmarks object from a list of raw bookmark string values.

    :param values: ASCII string values (raw bookmarks)
    :type values: Iterable[str]
    :return: Bookmarks object
    :rtype: Bookmarks
    """
    # Create an empty Bookmarks object
    bookmarks = cls()

    # Iterate through the values passed as parameters
    for value in values:
        # Check if the value is a valid bookmark link
        if re.match(r"^((ht|f)tp(s?)\:\/\/)*[a-zA-Z0-9\-\.]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,6}(\:[0-9]{1,6})?(\/[-a-zA-Z0-9@:%_\+\.~#?&//=]*)*$", value):
            # Add the bookmark to the Bookmarks object
            bookmarks.append(value)

    return bookmarks

def get_seq_with_type(seq, bufsize=None):
    """Return a (sequence, type) pair.
    Sequence is derived from *seq*
    (or is *seq*, if that is of a sequence type).
    """
    if hasattr(seq, '__len__'):
        seq = list(seq)
        type_ = "list"
    elif hasattr(seq, 'keys'):
        seq = list(seq.values())
        type_ = "dict"
    else:
        seq = (seq,)
        type_ = "single"

    if bufsize is not None:
        seq = list(seq)
        type_ = "list"

    return seq, type_

name: scale
docstring:
Get or set the scale of the graph.

If *other* is ``None``, return the scale of this graph.

If a numeric *other* is provided, rescale to that value.
If the graph has unknown or zero scale,
rescaling that will raise :exc:`~.LenaValueError`.

To get meaningful results, graph's fields are used.
Only the last coordinate is rescaled.
For example, if the graph has *x* and *y* coordinates,
then *y* will be rescaled, and for a 3-dimensional graph
*z* will be rescaled.
All errors are rescaled together with their coordinate.

name: hist_to_graph
docstring:
Convert a :class:`.histogram` to a :class:`.graph`.

*make_value* is a function to set the value of a graph's point.
By default it is bin content.
*make_value* accepts a single value (bin content) without context.

This option could be used to create graph's error bars.
For example, to create a graph with errors
from a histogram where bins contain
a named tuple with fields *mean*, *mean_error* and a context
one could use

>>> make_value = lambda bin_: (bin_.mean, bin_.mean_error)

*get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate
of a graph point created from a histogram bin will be.
It can be "left" (default), "right" and "middle".

*field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
must be the same as the dimension of the result.
For a *make_value* above they would be
*("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

*scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
If it is ``True``, it uses the histogram scale.

*hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

Return the resulting graph.

name: _verify
docstring:
Verify that *candidate* might correctly provide *iface*.

This involves:

- Making sure the candidate claims that it provides the
  interface using ``iface.providedBy`` (unless *tentative* is `True`,
  in which case this step is skipped). This means that the candidate's class
  declares that it `implements <zope.interface.implementer>` the interface,
  or the candidate itself declares that it `provides <zope.interface.provider>`
  the interface

- Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary methods

- Making sure the methods have the correct signature (to the
  extent possible)

- Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary attributes

:return bool: Returns a true value if everything that could be
   checked passed.
:raises zope.interface.Invalid: If any of the previous
   conditions does not hold.

.. versionchanged:: 5.0
    If multiple methods or attributes are invalid, all such errors
    are collected and reported. Previously, only the first error was reported.
    As a special case, if only one such error is present, it is raised
    alone, like before.

    This involves:

    - Making sure the candidate claims that it provides the
    interface using ``iface.providedBy`` (unless *tentative* is `True`,
    in which case this step is skipped). This means that the candidate's class
    declares that it `implements <zope.interface.implementer>` the interface,
    or the candidate itself declares that it `provides <zope.interface.provider>`
    the interface

    - Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary methods

    - Making sure the methods have the correct signature (to the
    extent possible)

    - Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary attributes

    :return bool: Returns a true value if everything that could be
    checked passed.
    :raises zope.interface.Invalid: If any of the previous
    conditions does not hold.

    .. versionchanged:: 5.0
        If multiple methods or attributes are invalid, all such errors
        are collected and reported. Previously, only the first error was reported.
        As a special case, if only one such error is present, it is raised
        alone, like before.
    """
    # Ensure the candidate claims to provide the interface if not in tentative mode
    if not tentative and not iface.providedBy(candidate):
        raise Invalid("Candidate does not claim to provide the interface")

    # Ensure the candidate has all necessary methods
    missingMethods = []
    for methodName in iface.namesAndDescriptions():
        if not hasattr(candidate, methodName):
            missingMethods.append(methodName)
    if missingMethods:
        raise Invalid("Candidate is missing methods '{}'".format("', '".join(missingMethods)))

    # Ensure the methods have the correct signature (if specified)
    for methodName in iface.namesAndDescriptions():
        method = getattr(candidate, methodName)
        methodSignature = iface.methodSignature(methodName)
        if not (methodSignature is None) and not (methodSignature == method.signature):
            raise Invalid("Method '{}' has incorrect signature".format(methodName))

    # Ensure the candidate has all necessary attributes
    missingAttributes = []
    for attributeName in iface.attributeNames():
        if not hasattr(candidate, attributeName):
            missingAttributes.append(attributeName)
    if missingAttributes:
        raise Invalid("Candidate is missing attributes '{}'".format("', '".join(missingAttributes)))

    # If we got this far, the candidate has passed all the checks, so we can return True
    return True

    """
    Verify that *candidate* might correctly provide *iface*.

    :param iface: The interface to check against
    :type iface: zope.interface.Interface
    :param candidate: The object to check
    :type candidate: zope.interface.Interface

    :type tentative: bool, default=False
    :return: True if all checks passed, False otherwise
    :rtype: bool
    :raises zope.interface.Invalid: If any of the checks failed

    methods = [{method} for method in iface.names(all=True) if iface.getRaw(method).appliable]

        if method not in candidate.names(all=True):
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f"{candidate} does not define method {method!r}")
        candidate_method = candidate.getRaw(method)
        iface_method = iface.getRaw(method)
        if not candidate_method.signature == iface_method.signature:
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f"{candidate} method {method!r} signature "
                                     f"does not match the interface signature")

    for attr in iface.names(all=True, only_attributes=True):
        if attr not in candidate.names(all=True):
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f"{candidate} does not define attribute {attr!r}")
        iface_attr = iface.__dict__[attr]
        candidate_attr = candidate.__dict__[attr]
        if not isinstance(candidate_attr, iface_attr.__class__):
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f"{candidate} attribute {attr!r} does not match "
                                     f"the interface attribute type")

    return True

def determineMetaclass(bases, explicit_mc=None):
    """Determine metaclass from 1+ bases and optional explicit __metaclass__"""
    # Check if explicit metaclass is provided
    if explicit_mc is not None:
        # Return explicit metaclass
        return explicit_mc

    # Check if bases is a tuple
    if not isinstance(bases, tuple):
        # Raise TypeError
        raise TypeError("bases must be a tuple")

    # Get metaclasses from bases
    metaclasses = [getattr(base, "__metaclass__", None) for base in bases]

    # Check if any metaclasses are None
    if any(metaclass is None for metaclass in metaclasses):
        # Raise TypeError
        raise TypeError("bases must have a __metaclass__ attribute")

    # Get the most derived metaclass
    return max(metaclasses, key=lambda mc: issubclass(mc, bases[0].__metaclass__))

def pop(self, key, default=__marker):
    """
    D.pop(k[,d]) -> v, remove specified key and return the corresponding value.
    If key is not found, d is returned if given, otherwise KeyError is raised.
    """
    if key not in self:
        if default is __marker:
            raise KeyError('{} not found'.format(key))
        return default
    value = self[key]
    del self[key]
    return value

def popitem(self):
    # Check if the cache is empty
    if not self.cache:
        raise KeyError("The cache is empty")

    # Find the least frequently used key
    least_frequently_used_key = min(self.cache, key=self.cache.get)

    # Remove the key from the cache
    value = self.cache.pop(least_frequently_used_key)

    # Update the frequency of all other keys
    for key, freq in self.cache.items():
        self.cache[key] = freq - 1

    # Return the key and value
    return least_frequently_used_key, value

name: isoparse
docstring:
Parse an ISO-8601 datetime string into a :class:`datetime.datetime`.

An ISO-8601 datetime string consists of a date portion, followed
optionally by a time portion - the date and time portions are separated
by a single character separator, which is ``T`` in the official
standard. Incomplete date formats (such as ``YYYY-MM``) may *not* be
combined with a time portion.

Supported date formats are:

Common:

- ``YYYY``
- ``YYYY-MM`` or ``YYYYMM``
- ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or ``YYYYMMDD``

Uncommon:

- ``YYYY-Www`` or ``YYYYWww`` - ISO week (day defaults to 0)
- ``YYYY-Www-D`` or ``YYYYWwwD`` - ISO week and day

The ISO week and day numbering follows the same logic as
:func:`datetime.date.isocalendar`.

Supported time formats are:

- ``hh``
- ``hh:mm`` or ``hhmm``
- ``hh:mm:ss`` or ``hhmmss``
- ``hh:mm:ss.ssssss`` (Up to 6 sub-second digits)

Midnight is a special case for `hh`, as the standard supports both
00:00 and 24:00 as a representation. The decimal separator can be
either a dot or a comma.


.. caution::

    Support for fractional components other than seconds is part of the
    ISO-8601 standard, but is not currently implemented in this parser.

Supported time zone offset formats are:

- `Z` (UTC)
- `±HH:MM`
- `±HHMM`
- `±HH`

Offsets will be represented as :class:`dateutil.tz.tzoffset` objects,
with the exception of UTC, which will be represented as
:class:`dateutil.tz.tzutc`. Time zone offsets equivalent to UTC (such

name: default_tzinfo
docstring:
Sets the ``tzinfo`` parameter on naive datetimes only

This is useful for example when you are provided a datetime that may have
either an implicit or explicit time zone, such as when parsing a time zone
string.

.. doctest::

    >>> from dateutil.tz import tzoffset
    >>> from dateutil.parser import parse
    >>> from dateutil.utils import default_tzinfo
    >>> dflt_tz = tzoffset("EST", -18000)
    >>> print(default_tzinfo(parse('2014-01-01 12:30 UTC'), dflt_tz))
    2014-01-01 12:30:00+00:00
    >>> print(default_tzinfo(parse('2014-01-01 12:30'), dflt_tz))
    2014-01-01 12:30:00-05:00

:param dt:
    The datetime on which to replace the time zone

:param tzinfo:
    The :py:class:`datetime.tzinfo` subclass instance to assign to
    ``dt`` if (and only if) it is naive.

:return:
    Returns an aware :py:class:`datetime.datetime`.
code:
def default_tzinfo(dt, tzinfo):
    """
    Sets the ``tzinfo`` parameter on naive datetimes only

    This is useful for example when you are provided a datetime that may have
    either an implicit or explicit time zone, such as when parsing a time zone
    string.

    .. doctest::

        >>> from dateutil.tz import tzoffset
        >>> from dateutil.parser import parse
        >>> from dateutil.utils import default_tzinfo
        >>> dflt_tz = tzoffset("EST", -18000)
        >>> print(default_tzinfo(parse('2014-01-01 12:30 UTC'), dflt_tz))
        2014-01-01 12:30:00+00:00
        >>> print(default_tzinfo(parse('2014-01-01 12:30'), dflt_tz))
        2014-01-01 12:30:00-05:00

    :param dt:
        The datetime on which to replace the time zone

    :param tzinfo:
        The :py:class:`datetime.tzinfo` subclass instance to assign to
        ``dt`` if (and only if) it is naive.

    :return:
        Returns an aware :py:class:`datetime.datetime`.
    """
    if (not getattr(dt, "tzinfo", None) and dt.tzinfo is None):
        # If dt is naive AND has no tzinfo, set the given tzinfo
        return dt.replace(tzinfo=tzinfo)
    else:
        # Return an aware version of dt
        return dt.replace(tzinfo=dt.tzinfo)
